quick: Motion sickness 25-50 mg 1 h before travel; vertigo 25-100 mg/day
With or without food; may take with food if GI upset
Commonly used for nausea; generally regarded low risk
Likely compatible; may reduce milk supply / sedate infant
summary: Meclizine is a first-generation piperazine H1 antihistamine with anticholinergic and antiemetic properties used to prevent and treat nausea, vomiting and dizziness from motion sickness and to manage vertigo of vestibular origin. For motion sickness the dose is 25-50 mg taken about an hour before travel; for vertigo 25-100 mg/day in divided doses. Drowsiness and anticholinergic effects are the main concerns, especially in the elderly.
indications: Prevention and treatment of nausea, vomiting and dizziness associated with motion sickness
Management of vertigo associated with diseases affecting the vestibular system

dosage.n: May repeat every 24 hours during travel

admin: Take orally about 1 hour before travel for motion sickness
Chewable tablets may be chewed or swallowed whole with water
May be taken with or without food; take with food if it upsets the stomach
Anticipate drowsiness - avoid driving or operating machinery until effect known
moa: Meclizine is a first-generation H1-receptor antagonist with central anticholinergic, CNS depressant and local anesthetic effects. It reduces vestibular stimulation and depresses labyrinthine function, blunting the nausea, vomiting and dizziness arising from motion and vestibular disorders; its exact antivertigo action is thought to involve central anticholinergic and antihistaminic activity.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to meclizine or other piperazine antihistamines
monitor: Anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation)

preg: Animal studies showed cleft palate at very high doses, but extensive human use has not shown a clear increase in birth defects; meclizine is commonly used for nausea/vomiting of pregnancy and is generally regarded as low risk. Use if clearly needed.
lact: Limited data; small amounts likely pass into milk. As an antihistamine it may reduce milk supply and could cause infant drowsiness or irritability; use with caution and monitor the infant.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is described. Use general caution in significant impairment.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment, as meclizine is hepatically metabolized.

major: CNS depressants (opioids, benzodiazepines, barbiturates) - additive sedation and respiratory depression
moderate: Other anticholinergics - additive dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, confusion
minor: Drugs affecting CYP2D6 metabolism - possible altered meclizine levels
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol because of additive drowsiness and CNS depression.
interactions.diagnostics: May suppress skin reactions to allergy testing - stop several days before skin-prick tests.

emergency: Severe anticholinergic toxicity with hallucinations, seizures or coma (overdose)

monitoring: Degree of sedation, especially before driving or operating machinery
Anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention) in elderly and at-risk patients
counsel: Take about an hour before you travel to prevent motion sickness
It can make you drowsy - do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you
Avoid alcohol and other sedating medicines
Dry mouth is common; sips of water or sugar-free gum can help
Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, prostate problems or breathing disease
pk: Effect begins about 1 hour after dosing
Approximately 5-6 hours (some sources up to ~14 h)
Antiemetic effect lasts up to 24 hours
pearls: Long duration of action allows once-daily dosing for motion sickness
Take an hour before travel - it works better for prevention than for established nausea
Strongly sedating and anticholinergic - use cautiously in the elderly (Beers criteria)
Distinguish vestibular vertigo (responsive) from other dizziness before prolonged use
Stop before allergy skin testing as it blunts the response
missed: For scheduled (vertigo) dosing, take the missed dose when remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, then skip it - do not double up. For motion sickness it is taken as needed before travel rather than on a fixed schedule.
overdose: Overdose produces exaggerated sedation alternating with CNS stimulation (especially in children), and anticholinergic features: dry mouth, flushing, dilated pupils, tachycardia, urinary retention, hallucinations, seizures and coma. Treatment is supportive - airway protection, activated charcoal if early, and benzodiazepines for seizures; physostigmine is rarely used.
